findings.title: `_require_instance` is duplicated across `markets.py` and `instruments.py`
findings.description: `_require_instance` has the same body in `markets.py` and `instruments.py`. Only the raised error class differs: `InvalidMarketError` in one, `InvalidInstrumentError` in the other. This is small and tolerable now, and the modules are deliberately kept independent. A third copy would justify a shared helper that takes the error type as an argument, for example in a private `_validation` module.

findings.title: `Market` accepts looser inputs than its annotations declare
findings.description:
The fields are annotated `tuple[...]` and `frozenset[...]`, but `__post_init__` accepts any iterable. This is documented in the docstring, and the tests cover lists, sets and generators, so I treat it as intentional. Two edge cases are not covered:
- An unhashable element in `adjustment_bases` makes `frozenset(bases)` raise `TypeError` instead of `InvalidMarketError`.
- An unhashable `source_bar_stamping` makes the `not in SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` check raise `TypeError`.

Both are only reachable with clearly wrong input, so this does not block anything.

findings.title: Validation, canonical identity and boundary tests are sound
findings.description:
I read `canonical.py` and `calendars.py` to check the diff against them:
- `markets.py` normalizes `session_calendars` (a tuple sorted by mode) and `adjustment_bases` (a frozenset). Order therefore does not affect equality, hashing or canonical bytes, and the tests assert this.
- The canonical encoder accepts `frozenset`, `StrEnum` and `Decimal`, which are the types these models use.
- `ContractTerms` rejects `bool`, `float`, NaN, infinity, non-positive values and bad currency codes. It uses `type(...) is` checks, and `fullmatch` for the currency pattern.
- Fixture calendar ids are derived from the calendar objects, so markets cannot reference a calendar that does not exist.
- `FIXTURE_CALENDARS` is a `MappingProxyType` keyed by `calendar_id`.
- The uniformity test runs one body over every fixture market. The golden vectors and import-boundary tests cover the new modules.

No swallowed exceptions, wildcard imports or magic defaults were found. Everything the new code touches is covered by tests. Each file is under about 270 lines.

structured_findings.summary: `Market` accepts looser inputs than its annotations declare
Validation, canonical identity and boundary tests are sound
